On the first floor there are porticoes, gabled on the sides and two-tier at the back. The colonnades are closed by gate balustrades, and under them there are numerous figures; Mau (cited in the bibl., p. 112, n. 8) counted ten of them, in various attitudes, and interpreted them, due to their white color, as statues, but the liveliness of the movements and the irregular arrangement rather suggest that they are real characters.

caption_en: 18. Triclinium (e), S wall, central section: the painting (1.37 x 1.06) depicts the exterior of a sanctuary enclosed by a pinkish boundary wall, with a dentilled frieze, from which hang garlands, details that are no longer legible today, interrupted by the door which, in the upper part, ends with gate elements. The right door is open and a donkey comes out. On the sides there are two aedicules, away from the back wall, under which are two statues. In the lower center there was the altar near which, on the left, a man makes offerings. Behind the boundary wall emerge plants with flowers and in the center stands an Ionic column that supports a pinax with the representation of the struggle between Love and Pan.

A bucranium hangs from the architrave, the frieze with rosettes (?) is pink and the roof yellow. The female statue holding a long sceptre in her right hand and a plate with an offering, perhaps a fruit, in her left outstretched, has blond hair surrounded by a wreath of leaves.

76. Cubicle (1), S wall with the window interrupting the middle area. The black plinth has a corolla in the octagon inscribed in the square placed at the corner, and a comic mask in the obverse one. The middle zone is red.

77. Cubicle (l), S wall, section E: detail of the black plinth. In the octagon inscribed in the square placed at the corner there are traces of a corolla. At the top corner of the square you can see the imprint of a cord stop imprinted as a guide line.

caption_en: 78. Cubicle (The), S wall, central section: detail of the black plinth. In the octagon inscribed in a square there is a Silenic mask.

79. Cubicle (1), S wall, central section: the compositional structure is modified compared to those of the other walls due to the presence of the door and the window. The frieze above the side panel is only partially preserved and has a goose. On the architrave of the aedicule rests a small picture with a mask that supports a floral spire, from above you can see hanging branches ending in berries, or feathers (?). To the left of the aedicule is a red partition with a griffin.
80. Cubicle (1), S wall, central section: detail of the black frieze with goose on a small plane, between low bushes.
81. Cubicle (1), S wall, central section: detail of the upper white area. Partition with a red background with a griffin rampant on the right.
82. Cubicle (1), S wall, central section: detail of the upper white area. The picture with a yellow background rests, with an acroterial function, on the aedicule with a comic mask.

83. Cubicle (1), wall O: Niccolini's reproduction renders the decorative details of this wall in full and with remarkable fidelity. In the plinth, next to the corollas of the side octagons, there is a swan in the central one. In the circular segments of the side panels of the middle area there is only one roe deer on each side; and in the friezes above you can recognize, on the left a pair of peacocks, and on the right two pigeons. The other details, also seen on the E wall, are still well preserved.
84. Cubicle (1), W wall, S section in current condition.
85. Cubicle (1), O wall, S section: detail of the red middle area. In the circular segment with a black background, you can barely recognize the tracks of the roe deer advancing to the left.
86-87. Cubicle (l), W wall, section S: details of the frieze with a pair of peacocks. The female is to the left of the bush that divides them, while the male is to the right.

caption_en: 86-87. Cubicle (l), W wall, section S: details of the frieze with a pair of peacocks. The female is to the left of the bush that divides them, while the male is to the right.

caption_en: 88. Cubicle (1), wall O, section S: in the upper area with a white background between the thin architectures hangs an oscillum in the shape of a comic mask, and thin shoots with bunches and flowers stretch out to fill the space. On the left the pavilion in perspective, with the rhytòn hanging.

89. Cubicle (1), W wall, central section: detail of the plinth and the middle area in its current condition. Despite the loss of some elements, in the plinth and in the predella, the central aedicule is fairly preserved, and only on this wall can you see the fine execution of the fluted columns with horizontal bands.

90. Cubicle (1), W wall, central section: detail of the black plinth. In the octagon inscribed in the square you can see a swan flying with spread wings holding a ribbon in its beak and with its paws.

91. Cubicle (l), W wall, central section: detail of the painting (0.43 x 0.40). A naked young man sits on the ground, turning his back to the observer, on a white fleece, he has a crown of pine needles on his head. He pours a liquid from a globular jar, to a handle, which a dog with yellowish fur, which is on the left of the composition, licks. In the background there are two other dogs of the same breed, also with collars, like the first. The pine crown has led to the belief that the young man depicted may be a Satyr, but he does not have sharp ears. No other replicas of this subject are known.

caption_en: 92. Cubicle (1), wall O, central section: the frieze of the architrave of the aedicule consists of a motif of rectangles divided into triangles, and with masks, alternating with rectangles with studs or quadrupeds. In the upper white area under the slender aedicule there is the motif of the picture within shoots, with hanging swings.
93. Cubicle (1), W wall, central section: detail of the upper white area. The picture on a red background shows a cupid on a chariot pulled by two swans.
94. Cubicle (1), wall O, section N: detail of the square placed at the corner with an inscribed octagon, containing a corolla, in the black plinth.

96. Cubicle (1), W wall, section N: above the black frieze with birds in the upper white area we find the thin architectural elements with the long branch with bunches and flowers, the oscillum in the shape of a comic mask and the pavilion with a red background with the window within which hangs a rhytòon.

98. Cubicle (m), N wall: in the center of the wall there was a niche walled up probably before the plastering of the wall because its presence is not reported by Mau (cited in bibl., p. 106) who, describing this room, says that the walls were covered up to 1.42 m "with brick stucco with black and red stripes, therefore white,  with leftovers of some rough painting".

3. In the cocciopesto plinth of the façade are preserved the engravings, made with a sharp object, to outline a rectangle of which only three sides have been completed.

caption_en: 11. Cubicle (c): the decoration of the wall E did not take into account the presence of the door, so the central compartment with a twisted candelabra is located near the latter. The picture on the side panel contained the depiction of a cupid kneeling with a hare. Above the upper area, with traces of the linear decorations, the holes in the beams of the floor are preserved.

caption_en: 10. Cubicle (c): the N wall has a bipartite structure with the panels of the white plinth, with a square placed at the corner, separated by a compartment with plants. In the middle area, equally white, there is a compartment in the center crossed by a golden twisted candelabrum, and on the sides panels with a hem of a stapled carpet in the vertical sections and semicircles and triangles in the horizontal sections. In panel O, preserved, there was a small picture with a cupid, facing de70

properties.name: Regio 9, Insula 9, Property d, Room c

caption_en: 12. Cubicle (c): the O wall, interrupted at the top by a quadrangular window with a sliding door to the left, in correspondence with which it has not been painted, retains most of the painted plaster, unlike the S wall in which, due to the almost complete fall of the plaster, the small picture with cupid holding a bird in his hands is no longer preserved,  seen at the time of the excavation (Mau, cited in bibl., p. 118). In the plinth, the sequence of panels with a square placed at each corner is reproduced here, alternating with compartments with plants; in the middle area the squares contained a swan on which there was a yellow toothed diadem, the edges of the carpet were lozenges in the vertical sections and triangles in the horizontal ones.

Triclinium (e), wall N: the room was once communicating with the procoeton (£) of the neighboring house at number c, through the door that was later walled up and not repainted, also because this modification was perhaps carried out during the first century A.D. when the second style that decorates this room was no longer in vogue. In section O you can recognize the traces of yellow orthostats arranged at the head and purple arranged at the edge.

Triclinium (e), S wall: the articulation of the interior space in the antechamber and hall is recognizable by the presence of a pilaster to the left of which, in the discolored wall, it seems to recognize the traces of molded cornices; in the room the yellow orthostats are arranged at the head, the purple ones by cutting.

caption_en: 18. Tablinum (f), wall E: of the painting (0.50 x 0.47), now totally illegible, the reproduction in the drawing of the German Archaeological Institute remains. The goddess, seated on a rock, adorned with rings on her arms and wrists, with a golden necklace and chirp, holds the reed lowered towards the water in which two fish dart, while a cupid, whose face was already lost, casts his line with his right hand (judging by the shape of his hand) and holds a basket in his left (but the designer had some uncertainty in establishing the action of the hands).

properties.name: Regio 9, Insula 9, Property d, Room f

caption_en: 20. Tablinum (f), S wall: the painting with Narcissus, already incomplete in the lower left corner, is documented by the drawing of the German Archaeological Institute. The young man's pose is the usual one: seated on a rock, and with the spit in his right hand, he does not look towards the pond in which his face is reflected; behind him advances the cupid with the torch held upright, which he will then turn upside down with the death of Narcissus.

caption_en: 23. Cubicle (g), wall O with walled antique hole: faint traces of the carpet edge of the N panel and of the central aedicule in the white middle area can be recognized.

caption_en: 24. Room (k), wall N: before being transformed into a kitchen, the cubicle had a decoration of the III style of which traces remain in the red middle area, which had a vignette in the centre, and was separated from the upper area, now discoloured, by a large band or frieze (?).

properties.name: Regio 9, Insula 9, Property d, Room k

caption_en: 25. Room (k), wall N: the vignette, made in oligochrome in yellow and blue, with a few touches of greenish in the most shaded areas, showed a small island dominated by a large sacred door that led to an enclosure with acroterial palmettes, at the bottom of which a Delphic tripod and a figure of an offerer could be seen; on the right a fisherman and two bidders.

properties.name: Regio 9, Insula 9, Property d, Room k

caption_en: 26. Room (k), wall O against which the kitchen counter with the boiler has been placed. The plaster retains traces of the fresco with a black plinth and a red middle area with a landscape vignette in the central panel.

properties.name: Regio 9, Insula 9, Property d, Room k

caption_en: 27. Room (k), wall O: the drawing of the German Archaeological Institute preserves the subject of the oligochrome vignette, with a tree around a column surmounted by an urn, near a sacred door around which wayfarers wander, including a woman with a basket and the bearer of a barbell, on the left a group of offerers around a statue.

caption_en: 28. Triclinium (1): the floor of the second style is in cocciopesto with rows of white crosses with a black central tile, arranged in such a way as to leave a marginal flounce without decoration.

29. Triclinium (1), N wall: a hole made by ancient prospectors has disfigured the E part of the wall painted in the III style, with a black plinth, aedicule with a black background, with a vignette and red border, in the middle area. The red side panels were crossed in the center by a narrow black compartment with candelabra and surmounted by a black frieze with small landscapes and still lifes with birds. In the upper area there were architectural elements.

30. Triclinium (1), wall N: in G. Discanno's drawing, according to a technique typical of that draughtsman, only the outlines of the figures represented in the vignette, which is already rather poorly preserved, are outlined. At the foot of a column, surmounted by an urn, sits a woman who holds the edges of her mantle with her right hand raised on her head and with her left near her knees. Two young men are in front of her, only partially covered by the cloaks they have on their left shoulders and each holding a spear.

31. Triclinium (1), wall E: on the ancient limestone loom structure, with a very wide texture, the decoration was laid with a symmetrical structure identical to that already seen on the N wall, preserved only in the lower half and in a condition of total illegibility.

32. Triclinium (1), wall E: the vignette of the central aedicule depicted, in one of the numerous replicas, the group of Perseus and Andromeda, in the version, known for example from the painting in the House of the Dioscuri VI 9, 6 (see vol. V p. 975, fig. 224), in which the hero helps the girl to descend from the rock to which she had been chained. On the right was depicted the ketos pierced by the young man's sword. Of Andromeda, who wore a dark red Robe, with a blue rim, the lower part was better preserved.

33. Triclinium (l), S wall: in the current conditions it is no longer possible to grasp any of the details visible at the time of the excavation and described by Mau (cited in bibl., p. 118) from whom we learn that in the frieze above the side panels there was a landscape alternating with a still life with pecking birds and that in the upper area there were architectures.

properties.name: Regio 9, Insula 9, Property d, Room l

caption_en: 34. Triclinium (1), S wall: only the vignette of this wall has been photographically documented in the late '30s, when the wall was in very different conditions. On the left we see Ariadne asleep on the seashore, near a column surmounted by a hydria, on the right is the bow of the ship on which Theseus will move away, who was in the center of the composition, flanked by Athena armed with shield, spear and helmet, now completely illegible, but already only partially preserved.  AFS C237

35. Triclinium (1), wall W in which, due to the presence of the doors towards the atrium and towards (m), only the central part corresponding to the aedicule with a black background with a vignette is painted. Numerous graffiti had been traced on it, perhaps corresponding to counts, still visible in the now discolored plaster.

36. Triclinium (1), wall O, central section: Io, recognizable by the horns on her forehead, seated on a rock, looks towards Argos who watches over her, leaning with her right arm and leg on the rock, while with her left hand she held the spear, according to the scheme known in the oldest replicas of the subject.

38. Cubicle (m), W wall: in the N section of the white middle area there was a painting, the subject of which is unknown, and the perimeter of which had been outlined with an incision in the already dry plaster. 79 N52604

properties.name: Regio 9, Insula 9, Property d, Room m

caption_en: 37. Cubicle (m), S wall: a narrow compartment with a yellow candelabrum is placed in the centre, between the side panels, a red horizontal frame marks the break towards the upper area, surmounted by the lunette, white like the whole wall and with a moulded stucco frame.

properties.name: Regio 9, Insula 9, Property d, Room m

caption_en: 1. Façade O in opus incerta, with door jambs in limestone blocks, and brick drain arch, originally covered with a high protruding plinth of cocciopesto, with an upper area of rough plaster. The large holes for beams indicate the presence of a balcony on the first floor.
2. Vestibule (a), N wall: a reduced flap of the high plinth with red panels separated by narrow yellow bands remains.  79 N52592

3. Cubicle (c), N-W corner: on the dark red plinth remains the yellow band that limited it at the top, and of the narrow yellow bands that articulated it into panels, only the one in the corner remains.
4. Cubicle (c): in the S-W corner you can recognize the recess for the bed, near which part of the high protruding plinth is preserved.

5. Atrium (d), wall E with the door and window towards the courtyard (e). Part of the high protruding plinth of cocciopesto painted in red with yellow stripes and the middle area of rough plaster remain. In the courtyard, moved towards the E wall, you can see the tuff altar, covered with white stucco, found near the small chapel.

6. Courtyard (e): in the SW corner a small sacellum was built, of the roof of which remain the holes in the beams above the white plaster on which a male figure with a yellow tunic with red clavii was painted, holding a palm branch and three tapeworms.
7. Kitchen (f), N wall covered with rough plaster and with the partition wall of the latrine leaning against it.

8. Triclinium (g), wall N: the rough plaster of the plinth remains; the middle area was divided into black panels separated by narrow red compartments, in the center there was a painting already not visible at the time of the excavation. Numerous graffiti and trowel marks are visible in the fresh lime of the preparation layers.
9. Triclinium (g), N wall, central section: a six-petal rosette inscribed in a circle has been engraved with a compass on the III style decoration. 79 N52535

10. Triclinium (g), E wall with the door to the atrium (h): while on the N section the III style decoration was preserved with the black plinth with plants, and the black middle area, the S one, like the contiguous S wall, up to the window, was covered with rough plaster, which did not allow us to establish whether the door towards (m) pre-existed or had been opened at a later time.
11. Triclinium (g), S wall, O section: a short section of the middle area with black panels with red borders is preserved. 79 N52536
12. Triclinium (g), wall W, with the window towards the courtyard (e): the painted plaster reached only a height of 3.90 m, while the upper part was in "rough white stucco".
13. Triclinium (g), wall O, section S: only the marks of the brushstrokes on the plaster can be seen where, in the black plinth, there should be a plant with a red flower and a yellow bird.

14. Atrium (h), N wall, section O: in the red geometric plinth you can recognize the articulation in panels crossed by a thin strip interrupted by squares placed at each angle, while straight squares are placed between one panel and another, in correspondence with the thin candelabra that cross the middle area on a black band.

15. Atrium (h): the large entrance 12 was evidently built with the transformation of the primitive house into an atrium, of which the cubicle (i) remains in the N corner, as indicated by the masonry technique adopted for the construction of the E wall. In the corner near the cubicle you can see remains of the red hoof. On the opposite side is the entrance to the stable (k). The two mouths of a terracotta cistern are visible: the one on the left (height 0.63, diameter 0.445) has a dentilled frame at the rim and a kyma cordon with impressions, at the base; the one on the right (height 0.55, diameter 0.39) with a double bullnose at the base was covered with white plaster.

16. Atrium (h): the fall of the plaster between the doors of the triclinium (g) and the kitchen (f), well preserved at the time of the excavation, so much so that Mau (cited in bibl., p. 239) observed "There are only a little better paintings between the doors of fe gtre red compartments to which are interposed two black stripes (the plinth is destroyed), which seem to be of the third style..." ,  revealed that the small size of the entrance to the kitchen is due to the narrowing of a wider passage.
17. Atrium (h), wall W, section N: detail of the red plinth with traces of a still life painting with a green branch with fruits.

18. Cubicle (i), N wall: the action of ancient cunicularii, attested by the walled holes and pedarole, visible in the upper part, determined the partial fall of the plaster, already incomplete at the time of the excavation and now completely lost. In the center of the white wall there was a vignette with a sacred door surmounted by vases, with t)jmpanoi and a pedum hanging, and a table; on the left, next to a tree, the herm of Priapus, an altar and wayfarers.

19. Cubicle (i), N wall: in the upper area were depicted two birds holding in their beaks the ends of a necklace with yellow globes that had three large red stones mounted in gold in the center. Of this motif six large circles remain graffiti with the compass. The similar decoration once present on the O wall is lost due to the fall of the plaster, like that of the S wall in which a bird was seen extracting a necklace from a box on which it was resting.

20. Cubicle (i), wall E with the window in which the imprint of the frame could be seen. The vignette, completely vanished, depicted a seated poet, with a crown of leaves on his head, the heptachord zither resting on his right leg and the plectrum in the left; beside him, standing, another male figure, with a less rich crown and seven-stringed claws. Below the holes for the beams of the floor, lined with bricks, you can see the trace of the low false ceiling vault that in the lunette of the opposite wall W

21. Viridarium (m): on the N wall, in which the window of the triclinium (g) opens, rests the flowerbed surrounded by a low pluteus covered with cocciopesto, while on the wall part of the plaster painted in red is preserved.

22. Viridarium (m): on the E wall, in the S section of the door towards the corridor (w) there are three manly figures, extremely schematized, especially the third which looks rather like a wooden trunk whose end is configured as a human head, and a helmet; above it reads Nasica Aug LX; as observed by Mau (cited in bibl., p. 246) it is a gladiator owned by the imperial house, who participated in 60 fights.

23. Viridarium (m): the S wall, with the doors of the rooms (s), (r), (q) and (p), is almost completely devoid of the plaster that presented itself with the red plinth and, in the O section, with the lararium painting of the Genius Augusti, toga that libated on a cylindrical altar, of youthful appearance and with the cornucopia in the left. Under this figure was graffiti EX SC. 79 N52540

24. Viridarium (m): in the S corner of the W wall there is the lowered arched lararium niche, covered with a layer of purple plaster to which a subsequent white plaster with a molded stucco frame and a red lunette has been superimposed. To the right of the niche was the depiction of the Genius familiaris who, accompanied by the popa with the axe, the Camillus and two female figures, is liberating on a tripod on which a container is placed.
1. Façade: on the doors of f and g the protruding balcony has been reconstructed. Modest edges of the plaster remain.
2. Atrium (b), S wall with evident restorations in opus vittata, of lesions caused by the earthquake of 62 AD.  '79 N52578

caption_en: 1. Caupona (a): near the N-E jamb in limestone blocks and uncertain work that constitute a short stretch of frame work, there is a small strip of rough plaster that partly covers a vertical terracotta pipe, the presence of which attests to the extension of the upper floor on this room. 79 N53610
